My new book, Co-Existence, is out today.  It is a guide to how to live & work in a world where AI is sometimes, but not always, better than you.

(And, for the release, I worked with Opus 5.5 to make a quite interesting experience for the book's website:

Folks who are very close to AI news on X tend to extrapolate too much from each new model. Anthropic went through a rough patch a few months ago with Opus releases before 5.5, and goodness knows that Google had a long dry stretch. 6.2 is not terrific but that doesn’t tell us much

Ha. When I had Astra 6.2 make a puzzle spy game using any setting it wanted, it set the game in "Bellwether Station." I thought it was an odd choice but didn't realize how deep a pattern this was. What a weird attractor for the model.

An illustration of both the power and issues with Astra 6.2 in a way that might be accessible: I asked it to create a game in Blender and Unity where you are the pilot of a Coast Guard cutter who travelled back in time to the War of Independence to stop the British invasion of New York.

It made incredible 3D models and a working game with no errors - its even fun to play! But Astra got obsessed with random ideas that didn't make a lot of sense and built them out without asking along with following my instructions: you could put down false buoys to lure the ship in the wrong direction (like the British would understand a modern buoy?) or you could persuade the British ships to go the wrong direction by talking to them, or that you would spend your time rescuing sailors from other parts of the harbor. It didn't even initially have a shooting mechanism until I pointed it out. This is all kind of minor stuff individually, but it was frustrating to have the AI constantly do its own things without telling me, given its instincts were often off, and then have to redirect it constantly. Other models, including GPT-6 Asta, didn't require the same struggle to control and operate. And these same issues show up in academic research and other more serious use cases.

The reviews of the early testers like myself of GPT 6.2 Astra is a good vindication of the continuing value of vibe benchmarks in addition to numeric ones. We lack good measures of  personality or perseverance or creativity or writing clarity or taste. But these things matter

It is a very funny time where the markets are basically assuming the future will look like the past even as many CEOs & AI observers & government officials keep yelling that the future is coming and it will change everything.

Efficient markets versus radical discontinuities?

OpenAI’s Dot is capable, but seems to be falling further behind in its interface compared to Muse and Duet. The single-threaded conversation, lack of inline generative flourishes (like maps), & the inability to see what tasks it is assigned makes it harder to use than the others.
I think contrary to many of our expectations, we have not seen a Fable class open model more than 8 months after Fable/Mythos was first made public.

As a side note, a couple years ago, making this benchmark & analysis would’ve taken a considerable amount of time in STATA, likely several days, and making it look this nice would have been quite a while as well.
